clue.text: Reactionary bishop has to move slowly

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to limp is to walk slowly and unevenly

explanation.surface: A conservative churchman finds he can only shuffle along at a slow pace.
explanation.walkthrough: Colonel Blimp was a British cartoon character, a pompous diehard reactionary; his name became a word for any such person.
explanation.definitionFit: A blimp, after the cartoon Colonel, is an elderly diehard opposed to change.

clue.text: Protection afforded by Prince Edward's armour?

parts.note: Edward of Woodstock was known as the Black Prince
mail is chain armour

explanation.surface: The chain armour worn by a medieval prince shielded him.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward the Black Prince was a 14th-century English heir; 'protection' is money extorted with threats.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackmail is the demand for money under threat, as in a protection racket.

clue.text: I would the French king were less busy

parts.note: I'd is the short form of I would
le is French for the
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone wishes the King of France had fewer duties.
explanation.definitionFit: An idler is someone more inactive, lazier, than others; here read as a comparative adjective.

clue.text: Spud gets in about last from drinking

indicators.note: about last says the added word wraps round the final letter of the spud

parts.note: spud is slang for potato
taken as written

explanation.surface: A potato joins in at the end of a drinking session.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's reading: POTATO 'gets' IN placed 'about' its 'last' letter O, so I-O-N ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: A potation is a drink, or the act of drinking, especially alcohol.

clue.text: Knocking about round pub without having a meal

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the pub letters sit around the meal
round asks for the word pub to be turned about and read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
having a meal means eating

explanation.surface: A drinker goes round the pub skipping dinner and getting into fights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns PUB into BUP, which then sits 'without' (outside) EATING: B-EATING-UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Beating someone up means assaulting them, punching and knocking them around.

clue.text: Refreshment announced for the pall-bearer

indicators.note: announced means the word for refreshment is spoken, giving a soundalike

parts.note: beer is a refreshing drink

explanation.surface: Drinks are called for the men carrying a coffin.
explanation.walkthrough: A pall is the cloth over a coffin, so the stand carrying it is the 'pall-bearer', not the mourners.
explanation.definitionFit: A bier is the movable frame on which a coffin is carried, under its cloth.

clue.text: Fluster me about oil for the car

indicators.note: fluster means throw into confusion, so the letters of me about oil get jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone panics about an oil problem with their vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: An automobile is a motor car.

clue.text: Tell is shooting well?

definitions.meaning: a player scoring freely is on top form

explanation.definitionFit: To inform is to tell; a sportsman in form is playing at his best.

clue.text: It secures slide showing larvae-eight of them, perhaps

parts.note: grubs are insect larvae
a rowing eight is a crew

explanation.surface: A microscope slide reveals caterpillars, eight of them.
explanation.walkthrough: A rowing 'eight' is its crew; 'larvae-eight of them' is a crew of grubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub screw is a small headless screw used to fix a sliding part in place.

clue.text: Drama on a Spanish beach

parts.note: a play is a drama

explanation.surface: A stage show is put on at a beach in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Playa is the Spanish word for beach, used in English for a sandy shore.

clue.text: Share beds

definitions.meaning: a portion or share handed out
a rented plot of ground for growing vegetables in beds

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain an allotment is a small council-rented plot where people grow their own vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotment is both an allocated portion and a small rented garden plot of vegetable beds.

clue.text: Rural deity with a list of animals

parts.note: a faun is a Roman god of the countryside, half man and half goat

explanation.surface: A country god keeps a register of the local wildlife.
explanation.definitionFit: Fauna means the animal life of a region, or a catalogue describing it.

clue.text: Form of combat among Ankara terrorists

indicators.note: among says the letters are found within the run of the words Ankara terrorists

explanation.surface: A style of fighting practised by militants in the Turkish capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Karate is a Japanese martial art of unarmed fighting with hands and feet.

clue.text: Divine grub or beetle

definitions.meaning: the food of the gods in Greek myth, grub being slang for food
the ... beetle is a wood-boring insect that farms fungus

explanation.walkthrough: 'grub' reads as a larva beside 'beetle', but here it is slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambrosia was the immortals' food on Olympus, and also names a family of fungus-farming bark beetles.

clue.text: Inexpensive steel blade for a penny-pincher

parts.note: inexpensive means cheap
a skate has a steel blade for ice

explanation.surface: A miser buys a bargain knife.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheapskate is a stingy person who avoids spending money.

clue.text: He hates us making a bangle out of a re-cycled hoop

indicators.note: re-cycled suggests the letters of bangle and hoop are broken down and remade into something else

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone turns an old hoop into a bracelet, recycling it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken by a Briton: 'us' means the English, whom this person dislikes.
explanation.definitionFit: An Anglophobe is someone with a hostility towards England and the English.

clue.text: N American climber with powdered head

parts.note: ground means crushed to powder
nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: An American mountaineer turns up with talc on his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climber' is a climbing plant, not a mountaineer: the American groundnut is a twining vine.
explanation.definitionFit: The groundnut, Apios americana, is a twining North American plant with edible tubers.

clue.text: A fine boy

definitions.meaning: in old Irish law an ... was the compensation paid by a killer to the victim's family

explanation.definitionFit: Eric is both a boy's name and an old Irish blood-money payment for a killing.

clue.text: Vehicle the French grab to get away, they say, from the eruption

indicators.note: they say means the assembled pieces are spoken, sounding like the answer

parts.words: Vehicle the French grab to get away
parts.note: a car for the vehicle, then bunk (to get away, as in do a bunk) with le, French for the, grabbing on at the end

explanation.surface: A car is grabbed by French people fleeing a volcanic eruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do a bunk' is British slang for run away. CAR + BUNK + LE, 'they say', sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbuncle is a large boil, an eruption on the skin.

clue.text: Black, when percolated, can be made white

parts.note: B is short for black, as on pencils
leached means filtered through, as liquid percolates

explanation.surface: Something black, once filtered, can turn white.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleached means whitened by chemicals or sunlight.

clue.text: Appear to see instant return

parts.note: lo, as in lo and behold, means look or see

indicators.note: return asks for the word for instant to come back, read right to left

parts.note: mo is short for moment, an instant

explanation.surface: Someone wants to view an instant replay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns MO into OM, after LO.
explanation.definitionFit: To loom is to come into view, often large or threatening.

clue.text: Not a dancing girl, but certainly beddable

definitions.meaning: a shy person left sitting at the side at a dance
a spring plant commonly used for bedding in gardens

explanation.walkthrough: 'beddable' teases a sexual meaning but just means suitable for a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallflower is both a partygoer left unasked to dance and a fragrant garden bedding plant.

clue.text: The Archbishop of Canterbury's church

definitions.meaning: both Frederick and his son William held the see of Canterbury

explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Temple names two Archbishops of Canterbury and a building used for worship.

clue.text: Studies the interior of geometric figure to make more compact

indicators.note: the interior of says the studies go inside the figure's letters

parts.note: a cone is a solid geometric figure
dens are studies, private rooms for working

explanation.surface: A mathematician packs work rooms tightly inside a shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To condense is to compress or shorten something into a smaller space.

clue.text: Mediterranean tree grown from seeds of custard-apples, russet or brown

indicators.note: seeds of means the starting letters, the germs, of each following word

explanation.surface: A Mediterranean tree has sprung from the pips of custard apples.
explanation.definitionFit: The carob is an evergreen Mediterranean tree with edible pods.

clue.text: Coleridge's dream place

parts.note: the setting of the poet's opium-inspired poem Kubla Khan, where a pleasure dome was decreed

explanation.definitionFit: Xanadu is the summer capital of Kubla Khan in Coleridge's dreamlike poem, now meaning any idyllic place.

clue.text: Oil for a sailor rounding the end of the Solent

indicators.note: rounding means going round, so the sailor's letters surround the final letter

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

indicators.note: the end of says only the final letter of Solent is taken

explanation.surface: A seaman sails round the far end of the Solent for fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: The Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and mainland England.
explanation.definitionFit: Attar is a fragrant essential oil, especially from rose petals.

clue.text: Exploited actress starts at the bottom

indicators.note: starts at the bottom means the opening letter moves to the foot of this down entry

parts.note: Eleonora Duse was a celebrated Italian stage actress

explanation.surface: An actress begins her career at the lowest level.
explanation.walkthrough: D, the start of DUSE, drops to the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Used means taken advantage of.

clue.text: Raise flag for golfer's approach shot

definitions.meaning: to hoist a flag up a pole
a low shot played to roll onto the green

explanation.definitionFit: To run up a flag is to hoist it; a run-up is a golf shot that bounces and rolls towards the pin.

clue.text: Showing good taste by dropping an opening number

indicators.note: dropping says letters are taken away from the word for number

parts.note: read as numb-er, something that makes you numb
the letters A and N at the opening of the word

explanation.surface: Someone demonstrates refined taste by leaving out a song that opens the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' means a musical item on the surface but is a drug that numbs; drop the AN at its start.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesthetic means concerned with beauty, so displaying artistic judgment.

clue.text: The last extremity is a little tender, perhaps

parts.note: a bit means a little

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word tender is only one possible arrangement of its letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The very tip is said to be a little sore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges TENDER into TEREND after BIT.
explanation.definitionFit: The bitter end is the very last point, the furthest limit of endurance.

clue.text: Listen to the morning song

parts.note: heard aloud, morning matches a word for grieving, so this is a sad funeral song rather than a dawn chorus

explanation.walkthrough: 'Listen to' signals a soundalike: the dawn song is really a song of grief.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a lament sung or played at a funeral.
